review_candidates.description: Company Name: ARS-Rescue Rooter Overview: The Azure Infrastructure Engineer is a hands-on infrastructure role that designs, builds, migrates, secures, and operates production Azure infrastructure extending our on-premises VMware and Windows datacenter. Focus areas: Azure networking, hybrid connectivity, virtual machines and platform services, disaster recovery, and migration execution. The role is DevOps-savvy, not DevOps engineering: the engineer uses Infrastructure-as-Code, Git, and pipelines to keep infrastructure repeatable and auditable, following and extending team standards. The engineer partners with Infrastructure, Networking, Security, Database, and Application Development teams and external consultants. Responsibilities Key Responsibilities Azure Infrastructure Engineering & Operations Independently design, deploy, and maintain Azure infrastructure: landing zones, management groups, VMs, storage, backup, monitoring, and governance. Troubleshoot connectivity, performance, access, and availability issues across VM, OS, network, DNS, firewall, and identity layers; perform root-cause analysis and implement durable fixes. Develop runbooks and operational standards; participate in incident response, change management (CAB), maintenance windows, and on-call. Hybrid Networking, DNS & Application Delivery Design and troubleshoot VNets, NSGs, routing/UDRs, hub-and-spoke or Virtual WAN, Azure Firewall, VPN Gateway, and ExpressRoute, including BGP and failover behavior. Design name resolution across Azure and on-premises (Private DNS, DNS Private Resolver, conditional forwarding). Implement private connectivity to PaaS services using private endpoints. Support application delivery with Front Door, Application Gateway, load balancing, and WAF, including TLS certificate lifecycle and failure-mode design when an edge service or policy fails. Work with Networking on firewall rules, IP addressing, NAT, and datacenter, branch, and third-party connectivity. Migration Execution Plan and execute VMware and Windows migrations to Azure: dependency assessment, Azure Migrate, lift-and-shift, test migrations, cutover, and post-migration support. Produce cutover plans, validation checklists, and rollback criteria; execute off-hours production cutovers. Support Azure infrastructure for SQL Server migrations (Always On to Azure SQL Managed Instance or SQL Server on Azure VMs). Maintain hybrid domain controllers, DNS, and AD integration for Azure workloads. Resiliency, Backup & Disaster Recovery Design and test DR using Site Recovery, geo-redundant storage, and region/availability-zone design against RTO and RPO targets. Operate Azure Backup and evaluate it against third-party backup and replication platforms for new Azure data stores; document and report recovery test results. Platform Services Infrastructure Provide infrastructure for App Service, Functions, Logic Apps, Service Bus, and API Management: VNet integration, private endpoints, identity, Key Vault, and monitoring. Support AKS at the platform level (private cluster, CNI, node pools, ingress, managed identity) with Application Development. Automation & Infrastructure-as-Code Build, modify, and troubleshoot Terraform following team standards: modules, remote state, environment separation, and drift. Use Git pull requests and code review; maintain Azure DevOps infrastructure pipelines, including approval gates and self-hosted agents reaching private endpoints. Automate operations with PowerShell and Azure CLI. Identity, Security & Governance Apply Entra ID, RBAC, PIM, Conditional Access, and managed identities to enforce least privilege and segregation of duties. Implement guardrails with Azure Policy, management groups, tagging, and Defender for Cloud. Partner with Security, Compliance, and Audit on PCI DSS, NIST, and CIS controls, remediation, and audit evidence. Observability & Cost Management Build Azure Monitor and Log Analytics alerts, workbooks, and dashboards; tune alert noise and logging volume; use Application Insights for tracing. Right-size and manage cost with Cost Management, Advisor, reservations, and savings plans, after establishing baselines. Collaboration & Cross-Training Share knowledge both ways: train teammates in Azure and cloud practices, and learn from them in their areas of expertise. Qualifications Required Qualifications Note: Candidates must demonstrate each item below with specific examples of work they performed as an individual contributor. Bachelor's degree in IT, Computer Science, Engineering, or related field; equivalent professional experience considered. 5+ years of enterprise infrastructure engineering, including 3+ years of hands-on production Azure. Hybrid networking: hands-on VNets, NSGs, routing, DNS, and ExpressRoute or site-to-site VPN; can explain tradeoffs and failure behavior. On-premises to Azure migrations: direct involvement in preparation, cutover, rollback planning, and post-migration support. Working knowledge of VMware vSphere, Windows Server, Active Directory, DNS, and Group Policy. Resiliency: Azure Backup and Site Recovery (or equivalent DR design) against RTO/RPO targets. Automation: working proficiency with Terraform (state, modules, environments), PowerShell, Git, and Azure DevOps infrastructure pipelines. Identity and governance: Entra ID, RBAC, least privilege, and Azure Policy. Independent troubleshooting and root-cause analysis of complex Azure issues. Experience supporting PCI DSS, NIST, CIS, or similar compliance requirements. Technical Skills Working knowledge Platform services: App Service, Functions, Logic Apps, Service Bus, API Management, Azure SQL Managed Instance, SQL Server on Azure VMs. Azure Virtual Desktop/FSLogix, Bicep/ARM, Defender for Cloud, and Sentinel. AKS, Docker, Helm, and Cosmos DB. Preferred Qualifications Azure certifications (AZ-104, AZ-305, AZ-700, AZ-500, AZ-400) or HashiCorp Terraform Associate; must be current. AKS platform operations, Azure SQL Managed Instance, or IIS/.NET application migrations. PCI DSS audit evidence, CrowdStrike or similar security platforms, and multi-site hybrid environments. Experience mentoring peers and using AI tools to speed scripting and troubleshooting. Work Details Remote; work day would be in Central Time Zone. Regular business hours with scheduled after-hours maintenance and cutovers, occasional incident response, and on-call as required; participation in change management (CAB). Occasional travel for project work, meetings, or datacenter activities.

Job Description Position Summary The I.T. Systems Administrator is responsible for the support, administration, maintenance, monitoring, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement of business-critical enterprise applications and supporting infrastructure within a complex manufacturing environment. This position requires an experienced, highly self-motivated IT professional who can work independently while collaborating effectively within a global IT organization. The successful candidate will support a diverse portfolio of ERP, warehouse management, engineering, manufacturing, analytics, and legacy business systems while ensuring their stability, performance, security, and long-term supportability. Working as part of the Enterprise Applications team, this role collaborates closely with Infrastructure, Network, Development, Data, Project, and Service Desk teams, as well as external software vendors and service providers. The ideal candidate is a strong technical generalist with expertise across enterprise applications, Microsoft SQL Server technologies, and supporting infrastructure platforms. The ability to independently learn unfamiliar systems and assume operational ownership of business-critical applications is essential. This position is fully onsite and reports remotely within a global IT organization. Key Responsibilities Administer, support, monitor, and troubleshoot business-critical enterprise applications, including ERP, warehouse management, engineering, manufacturing, analytics, and other operational systems. Develop technical expertise and operational ownership of assigned applications and services. Proactively identify technical debt, supportability risks, and opportunities for improvement across enterprise applications and supporting infrastructure. Contribute to projects and continuous improvement initiatives aimed at reducing technical debt, improving system stability, and modernizing legacy technologies. Troubleshoot issues across application, database, operating system, infrastructure, authentication, and integration layers. Administer and support Microsoft SQL Server environments, including clustered installations, Enterprise Data Warehouse (EDW) platforms, and related technologies such as SSIS, SSAS, and SSRS. Collaborate with Development, Data, BI, and DBA teams to identify and resolve database and application performance issues. Administer and support Microsoft Windows Server environments. Support Active Directory administration, authentication services, and Kerberos-related troubleshooting. Support and maintain virtualized environments primarily based on Microsoft Hyper-V. Support Azure-hosted business applications, databases, and analytical solutions. Participate in application and infrastructure deployment projects and ensure operational readiness prior to go-live. Review technical documentation and ensure supported systems remain properly documented and maintainable. Work within established ITIL processes for Incident, Problem, Change, and Service Request Management. Perform Root Cause Analysis (RCA) for recurring and business-critical incidents. Collect and analyze diagnostic information using tools such as PerfMon, Windows Event Viewer, SQL Server tools, Dynatrace, Spotlight, and application logs. Create and maintain technical documentation, operational procedures, incident reports, and Root Cause Analysis documentation. Collaborate with software vendors, service providers, business users, project teams, and global IT teams to resolve complex technical issues. Participate in regular remote meetings and communications using Microsoft Teams, email, and ticket management systems. Education Computer Science degree, Information Technology degree, or equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience. The Following Certifications Are Considered An Asset: IT Infrastructure Library (ITIL) Microsoft certifications related to Windows Server, SQL Server, Azure, Infrastructure Administration, or Enterprise Applications Citrix certifications Experience & Qualifications 5+ years of experience implementing, supporting, and managing enterprise applications and systems technologies in a complex, global environment. Strong hands-on experience administering Microsoft Windows Server environments. Strong hands-on experience administering Microsoft SQL Server environments. Experience supporting ERP and business-critical enterprise applications. Experience supporting ERP solutions such as Microsoft Dynamics AX. Experience supporting Enterprise Data Warehouse (EDW) environments and Microsoft SQL Server technologies including SSIS, SSAS, and SSRS. Experience troubleshooting SQL Server performance issues and supporting clustered SQL Server environments. Experience administering Microsoft Active Directory and supporting Microsoft Hyper-V environments. Experience working within ITIL-based support processes. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and troubleshooting skills. Ability to independently learn and support unfamiliar business systems and technologies. Ability to work independently with minimal supervision. Experience working with globally distributed teams. Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. Ability to create technical documentation, operational procedures, incident reports, and Root Cause Analysis documentation. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting manufacturing, engineering, warehouse management, and other business-critical enterprise applications. Experience with Teamcenter, NX, CAD/PDM/PLM platforms, WMS, OFS, TDM, or comparable business systems is considered an asset. Experience with Azure, Citrix, Linux, Docker, or related infrastructure technologies. Experience with Dynatrace monitoring solutions. Experience troubleshooting Kerberos authentication issues. Experience with PowerShell scripting and automation. Key Competencies Self-motivated and highly independent. Strong sense of ownership and accountability. Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills. Excellent communication and collaboration abilities. Strong organizational and documentation skills. Continuous learning mindset. Success Profile The ideal candidate is an experienced IT professional who combines strong enterprise application support, Microsoft SQL Server administration, and infrastructure troubleshooting skills. They are comfortable working in an environment consisting of both legacy and modern systems, can independently acquire expertise in unfamiliar technologies, and take ownership of ensuring the long-term stability, performance, and supportability of business-critical applications.
